# Project State — KrakenD Operator

> **Last Updated:** 2026-10-06
> **Status:** Conformance release: single-writer status with `Ready` conditions, a two-stage gateway reconcile, complete admission, a per-operation AutoConfig pipeline, per-object validation that excludes an invalid endpoint and applies the rest of its gateway, a trimmed, tested RBAC with metadata-only Secret and ConfigMap caching, and OpenTelemetry logs, traces and metrics. Unit and integration tests pass, 0 lint issues.

## Overview

Kubernetes operator that manages KrakenD API Gateway instances declaratively via Custom Resources. Built with operator-sdk (kubebuilder v4 layout), controller-runtime v0.21.0, Go 1.26. Four CRDs: KrakenDGateway, KrakenDEndpoint, KrakenDBackendPolicy, KrakenDAutoConfig.

## Implemented Systems

- **operator-sdk v1.42.2** initialized in `operator/` subdirectory
- Domain: `krakend.io`, API Group: `gateway.krakend.io/v1alpha1`
- Module: `github.com/mycarrier-devops/krakend-operator`
- All 4 CRDs scaffolded with placeholder types (default `Foo` field)
- Controllers scaffolded with empty `Reconcile()` stubs
- Full kustomize config tree generated (`config/crd/`, `config/rbac/`, `config/manager/`, etc.)
- `make build` verified — produces `bin/manager`

### Renderer (`internal/renderer/`)
- `types.go` — Renderer/Validator interfaces, RenderInput/RenderOutput, Options
- `config.go` — Core Render() method, buildRootConfig, buildGatewayExtraConfig (refactored into 6 helpers), ResolveImage, serializeJSON
- `endpoints.go` — flattenEndpoints (oldest-wins conflict resolution), buildEndpointJSON, buildBackendJSON
- `extra_config.go` — 3-layer merge (raw < typed < inline) for backend/endpoint extra_config
- `routes.go` — `PathParams`, `ConflictKey` and `RouteKey`: the route shape (parameter names erased, path cleaned) that the renderer, admission and the AutoConfig controller all key conflicts on
- `routecheck.go` — the route check: registers every route of the edition's copy in an in-process gin engine, in the order KrakenD registers them, and refuses what the runtime would panic on (the health path, `auto_options` clashes), stopping after 21 refusals
- `eewildcard.go`, `eestrip.go`, `eeonly_namespaces.json` — the EE wildcard rules (route conflicts stop after 21 with a notice line) and rewrite, and the CE fallback strip with the list of Enterprise-only namespaces (`CEDrops`, `EEOnlyNamespacesIn`)
- `routeadmit.go` — admits entries to the router oldest first; an entry the router cannot serve next to an older endpoint's is left out as an EntryConflict with Detail (router clashes, EE wildcard overlaps, auto_options)
- `validator.go` — `Validate` (`krakend check -t -n`, the full check of the gateway controller's whole render only) and `Lint` (`krakend check -n`: the admission checks, the gateway controller's root and endpoint checks and the AutoConfig precheck's group check), each after the EE wildcard rules and the route check; KrakenD CLI validation via temp file, validation rewrites EE wildcard endpoints to a parameter route and applies the EE wildcard route rule; the Redis pool is rendered under the EE `redis` namespace and validated
- `plugins.go` — buildPluginBlock, computePluginChecksum
- 60 tests, 94.1% coverage, 0 lint issues

### Config Check (`internal/configcheck/`, `internal/fieldindex/`)
- `configcheck.Checker` — the pod's one checker: `CheckRoot`, `CheckPolicy`, `CheckEndpoint` (policy-alone first; cross-namespace policies rendered empty for the quoted output), `CheckGroup`, `CheckRendered`, `Conflicts`/`NewClashes`, the `Memo` port (content keys), `Gather`, `SameConfig`, behind a fixed number of slots (`configCheckSlots = 3`) shared by the gateway controller, the AutoConfig controller, the policy controller and the admission webhooks. `LRUMemo` is the shared LRU `Memo` (the webhooks and the policy controller each hold one). `ValidatorVersion` names the minor version of the pinned binary
- `Verdict` and `EndpointVerdict` — what a check found (the output bounded, `Excerpt` for messages, `Masked` for the endpoints that lost an entry in the checked render) and, for one endpoint, why it fails (`EndpointInvalid`, or `PolicyInvalid` naming the policies)
- `fieldindex` — the KrakenDEndpoint gateway and policy field indexes shared by the controllers, the webhooks and the checker

### Controllers (`internal/controller/`)
- `krakendgateway_controller.go` — Primary reconciler, in two stages. Config stage: license evaluation → render → decide (`gateway_validation.go`: root alone, full check, each endpoint alone: all on failure, those that lost an entry on success; exclusion; safety net; `verdictMemo` per gateway, keyed on content) → publish an immutable content-addressed ConfigMap `<gw>-config-<hash>`. When the render is the applied config, only the endpoints that lost an entry are judged first, and the other checks run only if one of them fails. Infrastructure stage, always: SA, Service, PDB (the Deployment and the post-restart Job are held while the gateway does not control the SA), Deployment (mounts the applied ConfigMap; image of the applied edition; held while plugin ConfigMaps are missing), HPA, post-restart Job, Dragonfly, ExternalSecret, VirtualService; deletes the children of disabled features; GCs unreferenced config ConfigMaps. Watches the optional kinds whose CRDs exist at startup. Then inspectDeploymentStatus (replica propagation, ProgressDeadlineExceeded detection, rollout convergence: observed generation, applied config checksum on the pod template, and all replicas updated and available; a lost Deployment `Available` is mirrored). Mappers: endpointToGateway, policyToGateways, licenseSecretToGateway, pluginConfigMapToGateway (the last two receive metadata-only objects: the ConfigMap `Owns` and the license Secret and plugin ConfigMap watches use `builder.OnlyMetadata`). Reads Secrets and ConfigMaps live, never from the cache: the plugin ConfigMaps and the license Secret in full, the config ConfigMap's owner and checksum annotation and the garbage-collection list as `PartialObjectMetadata`, and a config ConfigMap's payload in full once per stored version (`verifiedConfigMaps`: UID and resource version, per gateway, in memory) to hash it against its checksum; the payload of any ConfigMap at that name is hashed whatever its owner or annotation, and a copy that fails is deleted (Warning event `ConfigMapTampered`) and created again. A render that passes validation but cannot be published sets `ConfigValid=Unknown/ConfigPublishFailed` (`handleConfigPublishFailed`), so `Ready` is Unknown, not True. Children of disabled optional features are looked up through the informer cache when their CRD was installed at startup, otherwise through discovery with a one-minute memo of an absent CRD (`absentKindMemo`), in the delete path only. Owns() watches for 7 typed resource types plus up to 3 optional kinds (Dragonfly, ExternalSecret, VirtualService) when their CRDs exist at startup. `Clock` field for timing. `detectDragonflyState()` sets DragonflyReady condition and `dragonfly_ready` metric. RBAC markers for dragonflydb.io, external-secrets.io, networking.istio.io. Writes each endpoint's `Accepted` condition for an applied render; derives its own `Ready` and phase.
- `gateway_config.go`, `gateway_rollout.go`, `gateway_license.go`, `gateway_optional.go`, `gateway_events.go`, `gateway_validation.go`, `verdict_memo.go`, `helpers.go` — the gateway controller's config stage, Deployment rollout derivation, license evaluation, optional-kind detection, transition events, the per-endpoint pipeline and exclusion signals, the verdict memo keyed on content, and shared helpers (`setReadyCondition`, `truncateMessage`, `UncachedObjects`, `CacheByObject`)
- `krakendendpoint_controller.go` — Resolves gateway/policy refs into `ResolvedRefs` and derives `Ready` and phase from `ResolvedRefs` and the gateway-owned `Accepted` (`api/v1alpha1.EndpointReady`); patches status with an optimistic lock, only on change; events on ResolvedRefs transitions. Watches: own spec and `Accepted` changes; gateway/policy create and delete. Mappers: gatewayToEndpoints, policyToEndpoints.
- `krakendbackendpolicy_controller.go` — Counts endpoint references (referencedBy); `Ready` (replaces PolicyValid): `False` from validatePolicy for a field out of range, otherwise the policy is checked alone through the `PolicyChecker` port, on a `CheckSlots` slot shared with the AutoConfig controller and a content-keyed `Memo`: `False/PolicyInvalid` with the policy's own bounded output, `Unknown/ValidatorUnavailable` (error returned, backoff capped at 5 minutes) when the check cannot run, `True` when it passes; observedGeneration. Built in `wireValidation`. Watches endpoint creates, deletes and spec changes (old and new refs on update). Protection finalizer `gateway.krakend.io/policy-protection` on every policy: a terminating policy is held (with a `DeletionBlocked` warning event) while any endpoint references it, and released after an uncached (`APIReader`) list finds none.
- `krakendautoconfig_controller.go` — AutoConfig reconciler: every reconcile fetches spec → loads CUE definitions → CUE evaluate → filter → generate → diff/create/update/delete KrakenDEndpoint CRs, converging owned endpoints on every run (drift repair, no checksum short-circuit). Ready derived from `SpecAvailable`, `Synced` and `EndpointsReady`, phase from `Synced` (the phase is empty before the first sync, then Synced or Error; Pending/Fetching/Rendering kept in the enum for compatibility but never written). `OnChange` resync every `defaultResyncInterval` (5m); `Periodic` resync at `spec.periodic.interval`. Watches: spec generation/label/annotation changes, owned KrakenDEndpoint spec changes, label changes, readiness changes (`Ready` status or reason) and deletions (`ownedEndpointPredicate`), `spec.openapi.configMapRef` and CUE definition ConfigMaps (a metadata-only watch: `configMapToAutoConfigs` reads names only). Reads its ConfigMaps and Secrets live: the CUE definitions ConfigMaps once each, in full, whose resource versions feed the inputs checksum (`loadAllCUEDefinitions`), and the spec and auth sources in full. Status/events written only when something changed. A stale-cache `Conflict` on a successful sync's status write, or a `Conflict`/`AlreadyExists` on an endpoint write, requeues quietly after 1s instead of failing (a failed sync whose status write conflicts keeps its own error/interval result); a transient endpoint write failure (`EndpointReconcileFailed`) or an unavailable config check (`ValidatorUnavailable`) always retries with backoff regardless of trigger; a failure to fetch or decode an external `$ref` document, or a fetch past the 2-minute deadline (`defaultFetchTimeout`), fails the sync closed the same way as a spec fetch failure (`SpecAvailable` and `Synced` False, reason `SpecFetchFailed`). An operation that fails CUE evaluation, the gateway config check or the endpoint write is held at its last-good endpoint (`Synced=False/OperationsFailed`, `status.failedOperations`, no backoff) while the others converge, and no stale endpoint is deleted while any is held. Ownership by controller owner reference (UID index), with adoption of label-matched orphans. `Checker`, `CheckSlots`, `MaxConcurrentReconciles` and `FetchTimeout` fields, and `Clock` for timing. Built in `wireValidation`.
- `autoconfig_endpoints.go` — AutoConfig endpoint convergence: `claimEndpoints` (controller UID index, adoption), `planEndpoints`, `routeCollisions` (desired endpoints that share a method and route shape: the one the renderer serves survives, the rest are held as `ConfigValidationFailed`), `precheck` (`routerClashes`, then `judgeCandidates`: root, group, each candidate; a hold shows only that candidate's own output or names the policy at fault, so another endpoint's value is never copied into status; CE-only namespaces held without a write), `writeEndpoint`, `deleteEndpoint`, `endpointOutcome.record` (raced, rejected or transient), `reconcileEndpoints` (the make-before-break pass), `creationOrder` and `withUncontrolled` (the renderer's oldest-first rule, with the stored age of desired endpoints no other object controls, shared by `routeCollisions` and the precheck's candidates), `recursRejection`, `endpointSpecEqual`, and the `AutoConfigChecker` port.
- `autoconfig_status.go` — `status.skipped`, `failedOperations` and `warnings` (at most 20 entries, messages cut at 256 bytes), condition message lists (`listed`: 5 items, then "and N more"), endpoint readiness (`summarizeReadiness`, `endpointsReadyCondition`), count wording (`counted`, `plural`), and recording a sync (`recordSync`, `syncedCondition`, `autoConfigStatusChanged`, `failureChanged`, `inputWarnings`).
- `schema_conflicts.go` — the `Accepted` message for an endpoint whose component schema differs from the definition the gateway publishes under that name (`SchemaNameConflict`).
- `suite_test.go` — Standard Go test helpers (testScheme, fakeClientBuilder, fakeRecorder) replacing Ginkgo+envtest
- `helpers_test.go` — 10 tests for conditionsEqual() covering both-empty, different-length, same-content, ignore-LastTransitionTime, different-status/reason/message/generation, missing-type
- 69 tests across 6 test files, ~84.8% coverage (filtered), 0 lint issues

### Telemetry (`internal/telemetry/`, `internal/tracing/`)
- `telemetry.Setup` builds the tracer, meter and logger providers from `OTEL_*` (export over OTLP only with an endpoint; a no-op tracer otherwise; a malformed OTLP header or endpoint variable stops that signal's export and is named, never quoted, in a startup warning); `service.name`, `service.version`, `k8s.pod.name` and `k8s.namespace.name` form the resource
- Log pipeline: every logger (logr, controller-runtime, klog, the stdlib `log`, grpc-go's `grpclog`, the SDK's own diagnostics on a stdout-only logger) goes through one `otellogr` bridge, a level processor (severity floor, timestamp and severity text, never-cancelled export context), a synchronous stdout JSON exporter and a batched OTLP exporter; errors are `exception.message`/`exception.type`, with no stack traces; `InstallGRPCLogging` and `InstallLogging` are the only globals set
- Instrumentation: `TraceKubeAPI` (client spans for requests sent under a span, trace context to the API server), `ReadEvents` (`k8s.client.get`/`list` span events), `TraceWebhookServer` (admission server spans continuing the API server's trace), `TraceExecutor` (a span per `krakend check`); background API traffic (informers, lease renewals, metrics-endpoint reviews, RESTMapper discovery other than the operator's own `crdAvailable` lookups, events) is not traced; optional CRD lookups in a reconcile are `k8s.discovery` spans
- `tracing.Start` starts a span and rebinds the context's logger so its records carry the trace and span IDs; `tracing.End` records an error and ends; `tracing/tracingtest` is an in-memory recorder with parent/child assertions; `tracing/background_test.go` guards against fresh contexts on request paths
- Spans identify objects (kind, namespace, name, generation) and record no spec values: a denied admission sets `admission.allowed` and `admission.code` and no status or text; no span carries a denial, a warning or krakend output, and the CUE and generation spans carry a fixed description
- `cmd/main.go` — Wires Renderer, Validator, Recorder, Clock into all controller setups; passes X509LicenseParser and the API reader to the gateway reconciler; builds the one `configcheck.Checker`, and the gateway, AutoConfig and policy reconcilers that hold it (the AutoConfig one with Fetcher, CUEEvaluator, Filter, Generator; it and the policy one share a one-slot `CheckSlots` bound), in `wireValidation`; sets `MaxConcurrentReconciles` from `--autoconfig-max-concurrent-reconciles` (default 4); and calls `webhook.SetupWebhooks(mgr, validators)` for admission webhook registration; `LeaderElectionID` set to `krakend-operator-leader`; `run()` sets telemetry up first (after parsing flags) and flushes it last, within 5 seconds; `wireValidation` takes `instrumentation` (the tracer and `OperatorMetrics`); `wireEndpointController` builds the endpoint reconciler; `--log-format` and the kept `--zap-*` flags (`logflags.go`); `main.version`, set from the `VERSION` build argument
- `cmd/webhooks.go` — `registerWebhooks` sets the webhooks up only when enabled and then adds the `webhook` readiness check (`GetWebhookServer().StartedChecker()`), so each replica is Ready only once its webhook server accepts TLS connections; with webhooks disabled it touches nothing on the manager

### AutoConfig Subsystem (`internal/autoconfig/`)
- `filter.go` — Filter interface: Apply with include/exclude rules for paths (glob), tags, methods (case-insensitive), operationIds
- `fetcher.go` — Fetcher interface: ConfigMap and HTTP sources, SSRF mitigations (loopback, link-local, ULA, RFC 1918), dual transport policy (strict/lenient), bearer token and basic auth from Secrets
- `generator.go` — Generator interface: wraps EndpointEntry in KrakenDEndpoint CRs, auto-generated labels, duplicate detection (path and method, operationId, endpoint name; reported in `Skipped` as `DuplicateOperationId`), sanitized naming (`SanitizeName`, `OperationEndpointName`), and each endpoint's schema closure with a warning per unresolved reference
- `operations.go` — `Operation` and `OperationIssue`: what skipped and failed operations report
- `parameters.go` — `DereferenceParameters`: inlines parameter `$ref`s (`#/components/` targets only) before CUE evaluation, warns about the ones that do not resolve, and fails past the 10 MiB body limit
- `jsonwalk.go` — the JSON walk, the example-payload rule and the name-keyed maps (whose members are objects whatever they are named) shared by the `$ref` resolver, `ExternalRefs` and the schema closure; example data is never fetched (only an Example Object's own `$ref`, and a root `$ref` chain in its target, is, and the target is inlined under `components/examples`)
- `schemas.go` — `ExtractComponentSchemas` and `SchemaClosure` (the component schemas an endpoint's documentation references, directly or transitively)
- `cue_evaluator.go` — CUEEvaluator interface: multi-file CUE definition loading, JSON/YAML/auto-detect normalization, environment injection via Unify (not FillPath, for hidden label compatibility), custom defs unification, per-entry errors (an entry that fails CUE lands in `Failed`, anything else fails the whole evaluation), definitions unified in filename order, override keys quoted and sanitized, ambiguous and out-of-range overrides reported, HEAD/OPTIONS/TRACE entries moved to `Skipped` after the overrides, exportEndpointEntries with _operationId and _tags extraction
- `embed.go` — `//go:embed cue/*.cue` embeds default CUE definitions in the operator binary; `EmbeddedCUEDefinitions()` returns `map[string]string`
- `cue/defaults.cue` — Embedded default CUE transformation logic, adapted from KrakenD-SwaggerParse endpoints.cue. Transforms OpenAPI specs into EndpointEntry objects with: path rewrite support, no-op output encoding, configurable timeout, auth-conditional header forwarding (Authorization, X-MC-Api-Key, Content-Type), header/query parameter extraction from operation and path-item, rate limiting extra_config (`qos/ratelimit/router`), full OpenAPI documentation extra_config (`documentation/openapi`) with description, summary, tags, operationId, query/param/request/response definitions including `$ref` resolution and `allOf` handling
- Controller falls back to embedded CUE definitions when the default ConfigMap is not found
- Uses `cuelang.org/go` v0.16.0
- 60 tests across 5 test files, ~94% coverage, 0 lint issues

### License Evaluation (`internal/controller/gateway_license.go`, `internal/util/license/window.go`)
- Evaluated in the gateway reconcile; single writer of License* conditions
- `license.Window` computes the stage and the next boundary; the gateway requeues at it, at least every 5 min
- Events on transitions; no writes to the KrakenDGateway object
- Handles expiry (with/without fallback-to-CE) and the 1 h safety buffer
- Recovery detection: clears degraded/expired conditions and emits `LicenseRestored`
- `readLicenseSecret` — supports both SecretRef and ExternalSecret convention (`{name}-license`)

### Webhook Validators (`internal/webhook/`)
- The CRD schema and CEL carry the object rules (license sources, OpenAPI port, single PVC source, post-restart script, durations and enums, the AutoConfig sources, Periodic interval and auth secrets, the endpoint map list, policy minimums), so the API server enforces them before a webhook runs
- Four validators (`NewValidators`): updates are ratcheted (an unchanged spec is skipped, a `gatewayRef`/`policyRef` is checked only when added or changed, a field rule rejects only errors the stored object did not have through `newErrors`; a changed sidecar probe or `runAsUser` is rechecked in full, endpoint entries match on (endpoint, method) so a reorder is not a change). A denial is `422` with a cause per field, a failed lookup or an unavailable validator is `500`, and the endpoint, gateway and policy validators, which run render checks, stop at a 12 s budget inside the webhooks' `timeoutSeconds: 15`
- `EndpointValidator` (`endpoint.go`, `endpoint_rules.go`) — `gatewayRef`/`policyRef` existence (a policy being deleted is refused, re-read uncached through `APIReader` before admitting), route uniqueness against the gateway's other endpoints with the same-controller exemption (`validateRouteUniqueness`), the entry rules (`validateEntries`: reserved and health paths, `/*`, unnamed wildcards and Enterprise-only namespaces on CE gateways, unknown placeholders), the `documentation/openapi.audience` shape, then `checkRender` judges the endpoint on its own; `refuseNewClashes`. The operator's own writes to endpoints a `KrakenDAutoConfig` controls skip only the render check
- `PolicyValidator` (`policy.go`) — `judgePolicyUse` per gateway (through the `fieldindex.EndpointPolicy` index); names broken endpoints; lints the policy alone, and refuses a new or changed Enterprise-only `raw` while a CE gateway uses it. Not registered for DELETE: the protection finalizer holds a referenced policy
- `GatewayValidator` (`gateway.go`) — the rules the CRD cannot decide: sidecar probes (when `spec.openapi.enabled`), `runAsUser: 0` on `postRestartJob` and `dragonfly`, a negative `tmpSizeLimit`. `authorizePostRestartJob` refuses (`403`) a new or changed enabled `postRestartJob` that runs as another ServiceAccount, reads a Secret (`envFrom`, `env` `secretKeyRef`), or sets a security-context field outside the `raisesPrivileges` allow-list (or a non-`runtime/default` AppArmor annotation) unless a SubjectAccessReview says the requester may `create pods` in the namespace (the manager role carries `create` on `subjectaccessreviews`). The render check refuses a new router clash first (`refuseNewGatewayClashes`), then judges the root alone, then the served endpoints together and on their own (`judgeServed`; on a create `warnWaiting` only warns). On a CE gateway it rejects Enterprise-only root namespaces and the typed fields `spec.redis`, `spec.config.documentation`, `spec.openapi.enabled` and `spec.dragonfly.enabled`, and a CE create or an EE to CE switch while any is in use. Warnings: `spec.replicas` with autoscaling, Redis pool settings that never reach KrakenD (deprecated timeouts, stored credentials), an enabled OpenAPI export or Dragonfly kept on a CE gateway, a `postRestartJob.workingDir` outside `/tmp` on a read-only root filesystem, and a `spec.version` whose minor is not the validator's
- `AutoConfigValidator` (`autoconfig.go`) — `gatewayRef` existence when it changes, the `documentation/openapi.audience` shape, two overrides for one operation (an `operationId` twice, or two that generate one endpoint name, `autoconfig.OperationEndpointName`), and a warning (at most five, then a count) for `policyRef`s that name no policy
- The shared `lruMemo` (`memo.go`) remembers the 256 most recent verdicts across requests, for the three render-checking validators.
- `SetupWebhooks(mgr, validators)` registers the four validators `NewValidators(client, apiReader, checker, operatorUsername)` built; `cmd/` `wireValidation` builds the one `configcheck.Checker`, the gateway and AutoConfig reconcilers and those validators
- All methods use runtime.Object with checked comma-ok type assertions

## Recent Changes

### 2026-10-06 — OpenTelemetry logs, traces and metrics

- Logs move from stderr to stdout, one OpenTelemetry JSON record per line (`--log-format=pretty` indents them); an error's text and type are the `exception.message` and `exception.type` attributes, and error records no longer carry the stack trace zap added. The `--zap-*` flags are still accepted.
- Each reconcile and each admission request is a trace, with every `krakend check` run and every Kubernetes API call below it; with no OTLP endpoint nothing is exported. Informer list/watch, leader-election renewals, the metrics endpoint's TokenReview/SubjectAccessReview, RESTMapper discovery (apart from the operator's own `crdAvailable` lookups) and events are not traced. AutoConfig spec fetches send no trace header and record redacted URLs.
- Metrics keep their names, labels, help text and buckets; a deleted gateway's reconcile-duration series stays until the operator restarts.
- A malformed OTLP header or endpoint variable stops that signal's export, not the operator. The final flush waits at most 5 seconds.
- Chart: a `telemetry:` block (OTLP endpoint or node-local collector, protocol, headers Secret, signals, sampler, resource attributes, log format); `POD_NAME` is set by the chart, kustomize and the OLM bundle.
- Dependencies: OpenTelemetry Go v1.47.0, Prometheus exporter v0.69.0, client_golang v1.24.1.

### 2026-10-06 — Per-object validation and exclusion

- Every gateway root, endpoint and policy is judged on its own; krakend check output is never parsed to decide blame, and is shown only to the owner of what was checked.
- A stored endpoint that fails on its own is excluded (`Accepted=False`, `EndpointInvalid` or `PolicyInvalid`) and the rest of its gateway applied; the gateway reports `EndpointsExcluded` and `krakend_operator_gateway_excluded_endpoints`. A root failing alone (`GatewayRootInvalid`) or a failure only together (`CombinedConfigInvalid`) keeps the last applied config. A validator outage excludes nothing and lifts no exclusion (except that a gateway that has never applied a config drops every `Accepted`), and the not-yet-applied wording of an exclusion appears only when the pass applied nothing new (`configResult.served` is false), while the gateway keeps serving its last config.
- Router clashes and EE wildcard overlaps between endpoints resolve oldest-first at render time: a newer entry loses to any older entry it clashes with, served or not (every older entry it clashes with is recorded as a winner), so deleting an endpoint can only bring other entries back, and a write can push an entry out only through a clash it takes part in. Admission and the AutoConfig precheck refuse a write that would create a clash (compared by loser, winner, method and path); the precheck looks again after any hold, until the result stops changing. Past 21 entries the router refuses next to older ones (an entry left in because its clash needs several older routes together counts too) the render stops resolving and admission and the precheck fail closed.
- A passing combined check vouches only for endpoints that lost no entry in it; an endpoint that lost one is judged on its own, on every path, so admission and the gateway controller agree on it.
- Admission: endpoint writes are judged alone (root and policy memo shared across requests); policy and gateway writes check every gateway first, then judge each failing endpoint with the new and the stored object and deny when any endpoint newly fails, even when another endpoint already fails, naming up to 20, with the names bounded by bytes (a denial found before the 12 s budget stands; none found and an unfinished scan is a 500). On a policy create the baseline is the policy with no content, so a referrer that fails anyway only draws a warning, while a failure only together is still denied. The withholding helpers, the whole-gateway ratchet and the naming reserve are gone.
- AutoConfig precheck: router clash holds, then per-candidate checks after a group check; a hold is cut to the 256-byte status entry; the rounds and attribution are gone.
- Verdicts are memoized by content per gateway and AutoConfig (output kept to 16 KiB; an inconsistent memo entry is a miss); a steady gateway runs no krakend check. The memo is in memory: after a restart or failover a gateway whose full render fails re-checks every endpoint serially on the gateway worker (about 0.1 s each at 500m CPU; about 50–60 s for 500 endpoints), once.
- The events are the gateway Warning `InvalidEndpointsExcluded` (when `EndpointsExcluded` appears or its message changes), the gateway Warning `GatewayRootInvalid`/`CombinedConfigInvalid` (when the verdict changes), and the endpoint Warning on an `Accepted` transition to `EndpointInvalid`/`PolicyInvalid`.
- Removed: the `GatewayConfigRejected` reason (API-visible), the `Attribute` helper and its source file, `RenderOutput.Sources` and the rejection memo.
- `config_validation_failures_total` counts only the gateway controller's rejections of a root, a policy alone or an endpoint alone, once per change of what it checks (the AutoConfig precheck and admission do not count); the controller's root and endpoint checks include the detected Dragonfly state.
- Known limits, documented: cross-namespace policy references need no consent (a referencing tenant can block policy updates and learn one bit about the policy); admission reads CE fallback from status while the controller decides it in the reconcile; admission renders no Dragonfly block; policy and gateway admission check an endpoint that already fails on its own before the endpoints together, so while it is not yet recorded as excluded a write that makes the others fail only together is admitted with a warning and the gateway later shows `CombinedConfigInvalid`; a large gateway with many such endpoints can answer a write with a 500 until the controller records their exclusion.

### 2026-09-28 — Conformance RBAC, caching and availability
- The manager ClusterRole is trimmed to the verbs the controllers use, pinned by `TestManagerRoleGrantsOnlyUsedVerbs`. `delete` stays on Deployments, Services, ServiceAccounts and PodDisruptionBudgets although the controllers never call it, because the `OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement` admission plugin requires it when an update changes an object's owner references (a gateway adopting a same-named object). The integration suite runs its manager as the operator ServiceAccount bound to the generated role, on a K3s API server with that plugin enabled, so a verb the role lacks fails the integration suite on the paths it runs; the golden test pins the role to the hand-kept table, and the VirtualService CRD is installed in the suite (Dragonfly, ExternalSecret and the optional kinds' `delete` rely on the table alone). The leader-election Role uses Leases only.
- The chart's ClusterRole renders from `charts/krakend-operator/files/manager-role.yaml`, copied by `make manifests` and gated by `make verify-manifests`.
- The OLM bundle is regenerated from source and gated by `make verify-manifests`: its ClusterServiceVersion now declares the four validating webhooks, the Job permission, 512Mi of memory and the node affinity of the kustomize install. Like kustomize, OLM keeps one replica with no PodDisruptionBudget or anti-affinity; only the Helm chart gets the availability defaults.
- Secrets and ConfigMaps are watched as metadata only and read live (`controller.UncachedObjects`). `controller.CacheByObject` strips annotations and `managedFields` from the cached metadata, so a client-side `kubectl apply` annotation never sits in the cache. Each CUE definitions ConfigMap is read once per reconcile, in full.
- Chart: metrics authentication RBAC, a `metrics-reader` ClusterRole and an optional ServiceMonitor; two replicas, a PodDisruptionBudget, soft anti-affinity and a render guard against several replicas without leader election. `/readyz` includes the webhook server (it does not cover cache sync: a request that arrives before the caches sync waits up to the 12 s budget, then fails closed with a 500). The webhook and metrics servers start their own certificate watchers from `CertDir`/`CertName`/`KeyName` (`cmd/serving.go`), which run on every replica, so standbys reload renewed certificates too.
- CI: a `krakend-smoke` job checks the pinned krakend binary's exit codes on three fixtures, and chart and fixture edits trigger the CI workflow.
- Docs: `docs/upgrade-guide.md`, `docs/runbook.md`, `architecture/README.md` (§14, §15) and `architecture/application/application-architecture.md`.

### 2026-09-28 — Conformance AutoConfig pipeline
- **AutoConfig pipeline correctness** — A problem in one operation stays with that operation: an operation that fails CUE evaluation, the gateway config check, or the endpoint write (an invalid rejection, a name another object controls, or Enterprise-only namespaces on a CE gateway) is held at its last-good endpoint, the rest converge, and no stale endpoint is deleted while any is held (`Synced=False/OperationsFailed`, `status.failedOperations`, gauge 0, no backoff). Writes run before deletes, every endpoint is attempted and the errors are aggregated, so an operation rename converges without a gap.
- Ownership is by controller owner reference (UID index): label-matched orphans are adopted, an endpoint controlled by another object is never touched, labels are merged. Before writing, the controller checks the endpoints it will write with the pod's one `configcheck.Checker` (`precheck`: at most 5 rounds, candidates carrying the creation time the cluster will give them (`creationOrder`), stale endpoints modelled as gone unless this pass keeps them (an operation held, or a write that the last status recorded as `EndpointRejected`), a baseline and a candidates-only isolated check for unattributed findings, `ValidatorUnavailable` when a check cannot run); desired endpoints that share a method and route shape are held by `routeCollisions`. The AutoConfig checks hold 1 of the 3 checker slots (`autoConfigCheckSlots`) and the gateway controller 1, so the controllers never hold more than 2 of the 3, and up to 4 AutoConfigs reconcile at once (`--autoconfig-max-concurrent-reconciles`, chart `autoconfig.maxConcurrentReconciles`) with a 2-minute fetch and `$ref` resolution deadline. Its precheck (rounds and attribution) is superseded: see 2026-10-06 — Per-object validation and exclusion.
- Status and readiness: `status.readyEndpoints` and the `EndpointsReady` condition (folded into `Ready`) follow the generated endpoints' `Ready` (a failed sync refreshes them too), and a label or readiness change of a generated endpoint triggers a reconcile. The `OperationsFailed` event fires only when `Synced` or `status.failedOperations` changes, and the full cause of every held operation is logged once per change per process (`logHeldCauses`). Count messages agree with their number (`counted`, `plural`). `status.skipped` (the five-method set: HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE are `UnsupportedMethod`; duplicates are `DuplicateOperationId`), `status.failedOperations` and `status.warnings` are capped at 20 entries of 256 bytes; the event that reported dropped entries is gone, replaced by `OperationsFailed`, `AmbiguousOverride` and `SpecWarning`.
- Overrides: an operationId that several operations declare fails the sync closed (`AmbiguousOverride`), so does a backend index out of range (`UnmatchedOverride`); override keys are quoted and sanitized (`SanitizeName`), so ids with `-`, `_` or a leading digit evaluate. Parameter `$ref`s are dereferenced, and spec problems (unresolved or colliding refs, undefined schema references) persist in `status.warnings`.
- Each generated endpoint carries only its schema closure, and a schema name that two endpoints define differently is reported as `Accepted` reason `SchemaNameConflict` on the later endpoint in namespace/name order (served, `Ready` stays True, no event of its own, only where docs are published).
- Docs updated: `docs/upgrade-guide.md` (the AutoConfig per-operation failures, ownership and readiness section, Pre-Upgrade Checklist item 6), `architecture/README.md` (§5, §13, §15, §16, §17), `architecture/application/application-architecture.md` (§2, §3, §8, §12, §13, §15, §16), `docs/runbook.md` (AutoConfig status, troubleshooting, alerts, scaling, audit lines) and `operator/README.md` (flags).

### 2026-09-28 — Conformance gateway reconcile correctness
- **Gateway reconcile correctness** — config stage / infrastructure stage split; immutable content-addressed config ConfigMaps with GC; render attribution (`RenderOutput.Sources`, `Accepted=False/GatewayConfigRejected`); per-entry conflicts (`PartiallyAccepted`, `status.conflicts`); EE wildcard validation by the EE router's rules; validation and image keyed on (checksum, edition) with `status.configEdition`; CE fallback strips and lists Enterprise-only features (`CEFallbackApplied`, `EEFeaturesStripped`); Redis pool rendered under KrakenD's `redis` namespace; license evaluation folded into the gateway reconcile; optional kinds watched when installed at startup; disabled features' resources deleted; `CRDNotInstalled`, `PluginsResolved`; `gateway_config_valid` metric; `Progressing` derived from the Deployment the pass reconciled (created, template written, template not the wanted one, old pods beside updated ones) instead of from change detection, with `RolloutFailed` honoured only for the current rollout; every independent child attempted and the errors joined, with `observedGeneration` held back while a child fails or the applied config's ConfigMap cannot be published; `rolling_restarts_total` counts template writes. Updated `architecture/README.md`, `architecture/application/application-architecture.md`, `docs/upgrade-guide.md`, `docs/runbook.md`. Its validation and rejection-attribution parts are superseded: see 2026-10-06 — Per-object validation and exclusion.

### 2026-09-28 — Conformance status model
- **Status model: Ready conditions and single-writer endpoint status** — Every kind has a summary `Ready` condition, a top-level `status.observedGeneration`, and `status.conditions` keyed by type (`+listType=map`); `kubectl get` shows Ready/Reason (Phase with `-o wide`). KrakenDEndpoint status has one writer per condition: the endpoint controller owns `ResolvedRefs` (`RefsResolved`/`GatewayNotFound`/`PolicyNotFound`) and `Ready`; the gateway controller owns `Accepted` (`Accepted`/`EndpointConflict`; `PartiallyAccepted`, `GatewayConfigRejected`, `SchemaNameConflict` and `EEFeaturesStripped` are defined for later use; a docs-only `SchemaNameConflict` keeps `Ready=True`), written on every endpoint of a render only once that render is the applied configuration, only on change, with events on transitions. Both write with `Status().Patch` and `MergeFromWithOptimisticLock`. `Ready` and `phase` come from `api/v1alpha1.EndpointReady` and `EndpointPhaseFromReady`; the legacy `Available` condition is removed, which ends the Conflicted/Active flip-flop. Gateway `Ready` and phase are derived on every reconcile (no latching: a revert or a recovered rollout clears Error; `ConfigValid` reason `ConfigApplied`); `observedGeneration` advances on a rejected configuration; `Ready=Unknown` (`ValidatorUnavailable`) while the validator is unavailable; the license monitor (since folded into the gateway reconcile) writes only License* conditions, with an optimistic lock. AutoConfig: `Ready` from SpecAvailable and Synced, phase from Synced, no initial Pending write, retry backoff capped at 5m. Policy: `Ready` replaces `PolicyValid`. Watches: the endpoint controller reacts to gateway/policy create/delete and to `Accepted` changes; the policy controller to endpoint spec changes only. Updated `architecture/README.md`, `docs/upgrade-guide.md`, `docs/runbook.md`. Its `GatewayConfigRejected` reason is superseded: see 2026-10-06 — Per-object validation and exclusion.

### 2026-09-28
- **Gateway validation, status and admission fixes** — (1) Config validation runs offline (`krakend check -t -n`) under a 30 s default timeout. (2) A rejected config settles: status is written only on change, the last rejected input is remembered per gateway, and `config_validation_failures_total` counts each rejected input once. (3) An unavailable validator is reported as `ConfigValid=Unknown` with reason `ValidatorUnavailable` and retried with backoff, instead of being reported as a broken config. (4) Condition messages are capped at 4 KiB, with the full output in the logs. (5) Terminating gateways are left alone, and per-gateway metric series and the rejection memo are dropped on delete or terminate. (6) Under autoscaling the HPA owns the Deployment replicas, and the gateway webhook warns when `replicas` is set together with `autoscaling`. (7) Admission admits updates to terminating objects that leave the spec unchanged. (8) New `--enable-webhooks` flag; the cert watcher is skipped when webhooks are disabled. (9) Chart `webhooks.enabled: false` works, `webhooks.caBundle` accepts PEM or base64 and is encoded once, and the no-op gateway DELETE webhook registration is removed from the chart and from `operator/config/webhook/manifests.yaml`. Its rejection-memo part is superseded: see 2026-10-06 — Per-object validation and exclusion.
- **Fix: AutoConfig conflict handling, endpoint-write backoff, and $ref fail-closed** — Three follow-up fixes landing in the same PR as the continuous-reconciliation work below. (1) Conflicts are no longer treated as failures: a stale-cache `Conflict` on an AutoConfig status write, or a `Conflict`/`AlreadyExists` on an endpoint write, now requeues quietly after `conflictRequeueDelay` (1s) — no error log, no event, no status change — instead of surfacing a raw reconciler error or (for an endpoint write) `EndpointReconcileFailed`. The exception is a failed sync whose failure-status write conflicts: it returns the failure's own result (the error for backoff, or the `Periodic` interval) with no event, since a `RequeueAfter` would reset controller-runtime's backoff. The buffered input-warning events (`CUEEvaluationWarning`, `DuplicateOperationId`, `AdditionalEndpointOverride`) are now emitted only after the reconcile's own terminal status write succeeds, so a reconcile that loses to a conflict doesn't re-emit them on its retry. (2) A non-conflict endpoint write failure (`EndpointReconcileFailed`) now always retries with controller-runtime backoff, on both `OnChange` and `Periodic` triggers — previously a `Periodic` AutoConfig waited a full `spec.periodic.interval` to retry what's usually a transient write error. (3) External `$ref` resolution (`ResolveExternalRefs`) now fails the sync closed on a fetch or decode failure of the referenced document: `SpecAvailable=False` and `Synced=False` (every spec fetch failure now sets both), reason `SpecFetchFailed`, message prefixed `resolving external $refs: ` (only for external-document failures; a main-spec decode error keeps its own message), last-good endpoints kept — previously this was a warning and the raw `$ref` was left in the generated config, so a transient failure silently changed the rendered endpoints. Pointer-not-found, cycles, and schema-name collisions between `$ref`s remain warnings. A relative `$ref` inside an external document now resolves against that document's URL instead of the main spec's, and refs are walked in sorted key order so the first failing ref is deterministic. Also: admission now rejects a non-list (or `null`, or `null`-item) `documentation/openapi.audience` inside `extraConfig` on `KrakenDAutoConfig` (`spec.overrides[]`, `spec.defaults.endpoint`, `spec.additionalEndpoints[]`) and `KrakenDEndpoint` (`spec.endpoints[]`) — message `must be a list of strings, e.g. ["internal"]` — and the default CUE definitions reject a non-list `audience` declared directly on an OpenAPI operation (`CUEEvaluationFailed`); a malformed value would otherwise pass validation and fail `krakend check -tlc` for every service on that gateway. New metric `krakend_operator_autoconfig_synced` (gauge, per `namespace`+`name`): 1 after a successful sync, 0 while the AutoConfig is failing (set before the failure-status write, so a failed write can't leave a stale 1); the series is removed when the AutoConfig is deleted. Updated `architecture/README.md`, `architecture/application/application-architecture.md`, `docs/upgrade-guide.md`, `docs/runbook.md`.

### 2026-09-25
- **Fix: AutoConfig now fails closed on unmatched overrides** — Previously, a `spec.overrides[]` entry whose `operationId` matched no generated operation was silently dropped and the sync still reported `Synced: True`. The evaluator now reports `CUEOutput.UnmatchedOverrides`, and the AutoConfig controller fails the sync when it's non-empty: `status.phase: Error`, `Synced=False` with reason `UnmatchedOverride` (message lists the offending operationIds), plus a matching `Warning` event. The generator doesn't run, so existing `KrakenDEndpoints` keep their last-good state until the override is fixed or removed; the resource is re-evaluated on subsequent reconciles until then. An evaluation-semantics version (`autoConfigEvalVersion`) was briefly added to `status.specChecksum` to force one re-evaluation of every AutoConfig after upgrade, then removed again the same day once every reconcile started evaluating unconditionally (see the continuous-reconciliation entry below) — that made the version bump redundant; healthy resources still see no endpoint churn (`CreateOrUpdate`). `applyFieldOverrides` now indexes operationIds in `Entries` order with the first occurrence winning, matching the generator's duplicate handling, so an override on a duplicated operationId lands on the published endpoint instead of a skipped duplicate. Also: the controller now emits one `Warning` event with reason `CUEEvaluationWarning` per evaluator warning (e.g. an operation skipped because it failed to convert) — previously these were collected but never surfaced. Updated `architecture/README.md`, `docs/upgrade-guide.md`, `docs/runbook.md`.
- **Fix: AutoConfig continuous reconciliation, drift repair and resync** — Four root causes fixed. (1) Status-write loop: every reconcile persisted a transient phase (`Synced`→`Fetching`, sometimes `Rendering`) then wrote `Synced` again, and `For(&KrakenDAutoConfig{})` had no predicate, so each status write immediately re-enqueued the object (~5-6 status writes/s per AutoConfig in production). The controller no longer sets `Fetching`/`Rendering` (kept in the enum for compatibility; observed phases are now `Pending`/`Synced`/`Error`), and the primary watch now uses `predicate.Or(GenerationChangedPredicate, LabelChangedPredicate, AnnotationChangedPredicate)` so status-only updates don't re-trigger. (2) No resync for `trigger: OnChange`: `requeueResult` returned an empty result, so upstream spec changes were only noticed incidentally. `OnChange` AutoConfigs are now re-polled every `defaultResyncInterval` (5m) in addition to reacting to watch events; `Periodic` is unchanged (`spec.periodic.interval`). (3) The spec ConfigMap (`spec.openapi.configMapRef`) wasn't watched, only CUE definition ConfigMaps were — both are now mapped to AutoConfigs via `configMapToAutoConfigs`. (4) No drift repair: when the combined checksum matched `status.specChecksum`, `Reconcile` returned before generating/reconciling endpoints, so a generated `KrakenDEndpoint` deleted or hand-edited out of band was never restored even though `Owns(&KrakenDEndpoint{})` (now gated by `GenerationChangedPredicate`, so endpoint status updates alone don't re-trigger) woke the controller. The checksum short-circuit is removed — every reconcile fetches, evaluates, generates and runs `reconcileEndpoints`; endpoint specs are compared by decoded JSON value (not bytes), so re-encoding/formatting differences alone don't produce a write. `reconcileEndpoints` now reports created/updated/deleted counts, carried in the `EndpointsGenerated` event message (`"Generated N endpoints (C created, U updated, D deleted, S skipped)"`). Status is written only when it changed, and `lastSyncTime` and `EndpointsGenerated` update only when inputs or endpoints changed. The `CUEEvaluationWarning`/`DuplicateOperationId`/`AdditionalEndpointOverride` warning events fire only when the inputs differ from the last successful sync's; a failed sync doesn't record its inputs, so they repeat on each retry of a failing sync whose inputs changed (a spec fetch failure emits `SpecFetchFailed` instead). A failure to create, update, or delete a generated endpoint now fails the sync with reason `EndpointReconcileFailed` (phase `Error`, `Synced=False`, `Warning` event) instead of being returned as a bare error while status still read `Synced`. A terminating AutoConfig (`deletionTimestamp` set) is skipped, so under foreground deletion converging doesn't recreate endpoints as garbage collection deletes them. Force an immediate reconcile: `kubectl annotate krakendautoconfig <name> -n <ns> krakend.io/resync="$(date +%s)" --overwrite` (any annotation change triggers one). Updated `architecture/README.md`, `architecture/application/application-architecture.md`, `docs/upgrade-guide.md`, `docs/runbook.md`.

### 2026-08-18
- **postRestartJob hardening (PR #25)**: securityContext/podSecurityContext merges now use a Kubernetes strategic-merge-patch (`k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/strategicpatch`) instead of a hand-rolled field-by-field copy, so future k8s API fields merge automatically; an explicit `podSecurityContext.runAsUser: 0` with no `runAsNonRoot` override now drops the inherited `runAsNonRoot: true` default (avoids a `CreateContainerConfigError` Pending-hang). The Job identity checksum (`resources.PostRestartJobChecksum`) is now computed from an explicit projection of execution-relevant fields (script, command, image, workingDir, env, both securityContexts, serviceAccountName, resources) via `hash.CombineHex` (two length-prefixed digests, not a bare byte concatenation) — **not** `json.Marshal` of the whole `PostRestartJobSpec` and **not** a 12-char prefix of the bare config checksum (superseding the 2026-04-21 entry below, which is now stale on that point). The Job carries two distinct annotations: `krakend.io/checksum-config` (raw, invertible config checksum, also used by `deployment.go` via the shared const) and `krakend.io/checksum-postrestart` (the combined identity checksum driving naming/idempotency). Added `spec.postRestartJob.workingDir` CRD validation (absolute path, length bounds) and `spec.postRestartJob.tmpSizeLimit` (overrides the previously-hardcoded 256Mi `/tmp` emptyDir). The status guard is now documented as "once per unique config + postRestartJob-spec revision, ever" (not "after every rolling restart"); a skip sets `status.conditions[type=PostRestartJobSkipped]` (not an Event, since the guard fires every steady-state reconcile) so `kubectl describe` explains the no-op.

### 2026-04-23
- **Fix: OpenAPI export now all-inclusive by default** — When `spec.openapi.audience` is empty (the default), the init container now strips `audience` arrays from a temp copy of the config before running `krakend openapi export`. This ensures ALL endpoints appear in the generated spec regardless of their `documentation/openapi` audience tags. The KrakenD CLI's default behavior (without `--audience`) silently excludes audience-tagged endpoints; the operator now compensates for this. When `audience` IS set, the original direct `--audience` flag behavior is preserved. Updated CRD doc comment. Added `TestBuildDeployment_OpenAPINoAudienceStripsConfig` test.

### 2026-04-21
- **New gateway feature — OpenAPI export + serve**: `spec.openapi` (KrakenDGateway) runs `krakend openapi export` in an init container and serves `/openapi.json` from a busybox `httpd` sidecar on a configurable port (default 8090). Port is exposed on the gateway Service as named port `openapi` but deliberately NOT added to the Istio VirtualService (local/in-cluster traffic only). Supports `audience`, `legacy`, `skipJsonSchema`, custom sidecar image/resources. New helpers: `buildOpenAPIPieces()` in `internal/resources/deployment.go`, `OpenAPIPort()` in `internal/resources/service.go`.
- **New gateway feature — Post-restart Jobs**: `spec.postRestartJob` creates a Kubernetes Job that runs a user-provided bash script after every config-triggered rolling restart. ~~Job name embeds a 12-char prefix of the config checksum → one Job per unique config revision (idempotent).~~ **Stale as of 2026-08-18 — see that entry above: Job naming now uses a 12-char prefix of a combined (config + postRestartJob-spec projection) checksum, and "once per config-triggered rolling restart" is now "once per unique config + postRestartJob-spec revision, ever."** Supports env vars, envFrom, pod annotations, custom SA/image/resources, backoffLimit, activeDeadlineSeconds, TTL. Only created once the Deployment has converged on the matching checksum (reads `dep.Spec.Template.Annotations["krakend.io/checksum-config"]` + UpdatedReplicas/AvailableReplicas). New builder: `internal/resources/job.go`. New status field: `status.lastPostRestartJobChecksum`. RBAC marker for `batch/jobs` added.
- **AutoConfig external $ref resolver** (`internal/autoconfig/refresolver.go`): `ResolveExternalRefs` walks the fetched OpenAPI spec, fetches every external `$ref` (absolute, or relative to the URL of the document containing it) once (cached), inlines referenced fragments under `components/schemas/<sanitized-name>`, and rewrites the $ref to the local form. A `$ref` held by an `examples` entry (an Example Object reference) is resolved in an example role instead: its target is inlined under `components/examples/<name>`, where `<name>` is the first free sanitized name (`name`, `name_2`, …), and is never walked except to follow its own root `$ref` chain. Accepts JSON or YAML fetched documents. ~~Failures become warnings (not fatal) logged by the controller.~~ **Changed as of 2026-09-28 — see that entry above: a failed fetch or decode of an external document now fails the sync closed (`SpecFetchFailed`, message prefixed `resolving external $refs: `); only pointer-not-found, cycles, and name collisions remain warnings.** Internal `#/...` refs and ConfigMap-sourced specs pass through unchanged.
- **Richer endpoint-level `documentation/openapi` CUE extraction**: `cue/defaults.cue` now emits `header_definition` (from OpenAPI `parameters` where `in == "header"`), plus `type`/`format`/`enum`/`example`/`examples` on query/param/header definitions, and `description`/`examples` on `request_definition`.
- **Strip upstream `servers`** (`internal/autoconfig/preprocessor.go`): new `StripServers` removes `servers` from the root document, path-items, and operations before CUE evaluation. The KrakenD gateway is the externally-visible server; upstream URLs must not bleed into generated docs/config. Wired in the AutoConfig controller after `ResolveExternalRefs`. Failures are logged and the raw spec is used as fallback. 4 new unit tests.
- Regenerated CRDs (operator, Helm chart, OLM bundle) and deepcopy. Added 21 new unit tests (5 resources, 6 controller, 10 autoconfig). Lint clean. `go test -race ./...` passes for all non-e2e packages.

- Webhooks enabled by default (`webhooks.enabled=true`, `webhooks.certManager.enabled=true`); can be disabled or used with external CA bundle
- CRDs in `crds/` directory (auto-installed by Helm)
- Availability defaults: `replicaCount: 2`; a PodDisruptionBudget (`podDisruptionBudget.enabled`, default `true`, `maxUnavailable: 1`, selecting only the operator's own selector labels) rendered only when `replicaCount` > 1, so a single replica never blocks a node drain; soft pod anti-affinity (`preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`, hostname topology) when `affinity` is empty, replaced by a user-supplied `affinity`; `deployment.yaml` fails the render for `replicaCount` > 1 with `leaderElection.enabled: false` (two active controllers would fight over every object). The render test pins each, including the refusal (`expect_render_fails`)
- Configurable: image, replicas, resources, security context, probes, affinity, tolerations, webhooks, cert-manager
- Validated: `helm lint` + `helm template` pass

### CI Pipelines (`.github/workflows/`)
- `ci.yml` — PR-only gate: lint (golangci-lint v2.11.4), test (race, coverage >=80%, `make test-audit`), manifests drift (`make verify-manifests`: CRDs, RBAC, webhooks, the chart copies and the OLM bundle), build, integration (K3s), e2e (testcontainers + K3s); triggers on `operator/**` changes; also triggers on `charts/krakend-operator/**` and `.github/krakend-smoke/**`, so a hand edit of the chart's generated copies (CRDs, `files/manager-role.yaml`) fails Manifests Drift. `krakend-smoke` job: runs `krakend check -t -n` from the Dockerfile-pinned `KRAKEND_IMAGE` with `--network=none` on three fixtures in `.github/krakend-smoke/` and asserts exit codes (valid 0, decoding error 1, route conflict 1)
- `helm-ci.yml` — PR-only gate: Helm lint + template + render tests (`.github/scripts/chart-render-test.sh`); triggers on `charts/**`, `operator/config/rbac/**`, `operator/config/manager/**`, `operator/config/webhook/**` and its own workflow and script (the render tests read those config files)
- `release.yml` — On push to main: runs lint/test/build/e2e/helm-lint gates, then auto-calculates next semver from conventional commits (`mathieudutour/github-tag-action`), builds+pushes multi-arch image to GHCR, releases Helm chart via chart-releaser-action, creates GitHub release with changelog

### Operational Documentation (`docs/`)
- `runbook.md` — Health checks, Prometheus metrics, alerts, tracing, gateway lifecycle phases, troubleshooting, scaling, backup/recovery, log analysis
- `upgrade-guide.md` — Pre-upgrade checklist, Helm/kustomize upgrade, CRD updates, rollback, version compatibility
- Root `README.md` — Quick start, install instructions, development guide

## Architectural Decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| `operator/` as Go module root | operator-sdk requires an empty directory; repo root contains `architecture/` |
| operator-sdk over raw kubebuilder | Provides OLM bundle, scorecard, and additional scaffolding |
| Binary name `manager` | Default operator-sdk convention; architecture updated to match |
| `cmd/main.go` (not `cmd/operator/main.go`) | operator-sdk default layout; architecture updated to match |
| Blame by isolation | An object is invalid when it fails on its own; rules spanning objects (route uniqueness, router clashes, EE overlaps) are decided in Go by identity, oldest first |
| Mutate-function pattern for builders | Pure functions that modify objects in place, used with `controllerutil.CreateOrUpdate` |
| `unstructured.Unstructured` for external CRDs | Avoids pulling in heavy third-party Go types (dragonflydb-operator, istio, external-secrets) that upgrade controller-runtime/k8s |
| CUE Unify instead of FillPath for hidden labels | `cue.ParsePath("_spec")` rejects hidden labels in CUE v0.16.0; Unify with compiled CUE strings works correctly |
| Embedded CUE definitions with ConfigMap fallback | Default CUE definitions are embedded in the operator binary per architecture §16; controller uses ConfigMap CUE defs when available, falls back to embedded defs when ConfigMap not found |
| CUE adapted from KrakenD-SwaggerParse | Default CUE transformation logic faithfully adapted from the production-vetted KrakenD-SwaggerParse `endpoints.cue`, adapted to produce EndpointEntry objects instead of raw KrakenD JSON |

## Technical Debt / Known Issues

- Architecture §17 specifies `licenseExpiryDays` metric name but `promlinter` enforces Prometheus base-unit convention (seconds). Metric kept as `license_expiry_seconds` per Prometheus best practice.
- Architecture §2 scheme registration shows typed external CRD imports (dragonflyv1alpha1, esv1, istiov1), but implementation uses `unstructured.Unstructured` per architectural decision to avoid heavy dependency chains. Watches use unstructured GVK objects.
- E2e tests require rootful podman machine (rootless can't delegate cgroup v2 for K3s). SSH tunnel: `ssh -i ~/.ssh/rootful-machine -p 41941 -nNT -L /tmp/podman-rootful.sock:/run/podman/podman.sock root@127.0.0.1`
- The Enterprise-only `extra_config` list (`internal/renderer/eeonly_namespaces.json`) is taken from the KrakenD 2.13 Enterprise documentation and may need expansion as KrakenD adds Enterprise-only namespaces
